source_text: Ὁ μὲν οὖν Ἰησοῦς ἐπιστρέφων τοὺς μαθητὰς οὐχὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ [μὴ] προσέχειν ἁπαξαπλῶς γόησι καὶ τοῖς ἐπαγγελλομένοις δι᾿ οἱασδήποτε ὁδοῦ ποιεῖν τεράστια (οὐ γὰρ ἐδέοντο τούτου οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ) ἀλλ᾿ ἀπὸ τοῦ τοῖς ἀναγορεύουσιν ἑαυτοὺς εἶναι τὸν Χριστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πειρωμένοις διά τινων φαντασιῶν πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς ἐπιστρέφειν τοὺς Ἰησοῦ μαθητὰς ὅπου μὲν εἶπε· „τότε ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· ἰδοὺ ὧδε ὁ Χριστὸς ἢ ὧδε, μὴ πιστεύετε. ἐγερθήσονται γὰρ ψευδόχριστοι καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται καὶ δώσουσι σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα μεγάλα. ὥστε πλανᾶσθαι εἰ δυνατὸν καὶ τοὺς ἐκλεκτούς. ἰδοὺ προείρηκα ὑμῖν. ἐὰν οὖν εἴπωσιν ὑμῖν· ἰδοὺ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἐστὶ, μὴ ἐξέλθητε· ἰδοὺ ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις, μὴ πιστεύσητε. ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ ἀστραπὴ ἐξέρχεται ἀπ᾿ ἀνατολῶν καὶ φαίνεται ἕως δυσμῶν, οὕτως ἔσται ἡ παρουσία τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου“· ὅπου δέ· „πολλοὶ ἐροῦσί μοι ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ· κύριε, κύριε, οὐ τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἐφάγομεν καὶ τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἐπίομεν καὶ τῷ ὀνόματί σου δαιμόνια ἐξεβάλομεν καὶ δυνάμεις πολλὰς ἐποιήσαμεν; καὶ ἐρῶ αὐτοῖς· ἀποχωρεῖτε ἀπ᾿ ἐμοῦ. ὅτι ἐστὲ ἐργάται ἀδικίας.“ ὁ δὲ Κέλσος κοινοποιῆσαι βουλόμενος τὰ τεράστια τοῦ Ἰησοῦ πρὸς τὴν ἐν ἀνθρώποις γοητείαν φησὶν αὐταῖς λέξεσιν· ὦ φῶς καὶ ἀλήθεια, τῇ αὐτοῦ φωνῇ διαῤῥήδην ἐξαγορεύει, καθὰ καὶ ὑμεῖς συγγεγράφατε, διότι παρέσονται ὑμῖν καὶ ἕτεροι δυνάμεσιν ὁμοίαις χρώμενοι, κακοὶ καὶ γόητες, καὶ σατανᾶν τινα τοιαῦτα παραμηχανώμενον ὀνομάζει· ᾥστ᾿ οὐδὲ αὐτὸς ἔξαρνός ἐστιν, ὡς ταῦτά γε οὐδὲν θεῖον ἀλλὰ πονηρῶν ἐστιν ἔργα. βιαζόμενος δὲ ὑπὸ τῆς ἀληθείας ὁμοῦ καὶ τὰ τῶν ἄλλων ἀπεκάλυψε καὶ τὰ καθ᾿ αὑτὸν ἤλεγξε. πῶς οὖν οὐ σχέτλιον ἀπὸ τῶν αὐτῶν ἔργων τὸν μὲν θεὸν τοὺς δὲ γόητας ἡγεῖσθαι; τί γὰρ μᾶλλον ἀπό γε τούτων τοὺς ἄλλους πονηροὺς ἢ τοῦτον νομιστέον αὐτῷ χρωμένους μάρτυρι; ταῦτα μέν γε καὶ αὐτὸς ὡμολόγησεν οὐχὶ θείας φύσεως ἀλλ᾿ ἀπατεώνων τινῶν καὶ παμπονήρων εἶναι γνωρίσματα. ὅρα δὴ εἰ μὴ ἐν τούτοις σαφῶς ὁ Κέλσος ἐλέγχεται κακουργῶν τὸν λόγον, ἄλλο μὲν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ λέγοντος περὶ τῶν ποιησόντων „σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα,“ ἄλλο δὲ τοῦ παρὰ τῷ Κέλσῳ Ἰουδαίου φάσκοντος. καὶ γὰρ εἰ μὲν ἁπλῶς τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἔλεγεν Ἰησοῦς φυλάσσεσθαι τοὺς τὰ τεράστια ἐπαγγελλομένους οὐ παρατιθέμενος, τί φήσουσιν ἑαυτοὺς εἶναι, τάχα χώραν εἶχεν ἂν ἡ ὑπόνοια αὐτοῦ· ἐπεὶ δ᾿ ἀφ᾿ ὧν θέλει ἡμᾶς φυλάσσεσθαι ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐπαγγέλλονται εἶναι „ὁ Χριστὸς,“ ὅπερ οὐ ποιοῦσιν οἱ γόητες, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ βιοῦντας κακῶς φησι τινὰς δυνάμεις ποιήσειν καὶ δαίμονας ἀποβαλεῖν ἀνθρώπων· μᾶλλον δ᾿, εἰ δεῖ οὕτως εἰπεῖν, ἀποκηρύσσεται μὲν τῶν κατὰ τὸν τόπον ἡ γοητεία καὶ πᾶσα ἡ κατ᾿ αὐτῶν ὑπόνοια, εἰσάγεται δὲ ἡ θειότης τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ θειότης τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, ὅτι δυνατόν τινα τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ χρησάμενον καὶ οὐκ οἶδ᾿ ὅπως ἐνεργηθέντα ὑπό τινος δυνάμεως πρὸς τὸ προσποιήσασθαι, ὅτι αὐτὸς εἴη ὁ Χριστὸς, δοκεῖν τὰ παραπλήσια ἐπιτελεῖν τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ ἄλλους τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ τὰ ὡσπερεὶ παραπλήσια τοῖς γνησίοις αὐτοῦ μαθηταῖς.
pass_a_gloss: The Jesus, therefore, turning the disciples away not from the not giving heed at all to magicians and to the ones promising through whatever kind of way to perform great deeds (for his disciples were not in need of this) but from the ones proclaiming themselves to be the Christ of God and attempting through some fantasies to turn the disciples of Jesus away to themselves, where he said: 'Then if someone says to you: Behold, here is the Christ or there, do not believe. For false christs and false prophets will arise and will give great signs and wonders, so as to deceive, if possible, even the elect. Behold, I have told you beforehand. If therefore they say to you: Behold, he is in the wilderness, do not go out; behold, he is in the inner rooms, do not believe. For just as the lightning comes out from the east and shines as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.' And where: 'Many will say to me on that day: Lord, Lord, did we not eat in your name and drink in your name and cast out demons in your name and perform many mighty works? And I will say to them: Depart from me, for you are workers of lawlessness.' But Celsus, wanting to make common the great deeds of Jesus with the magic among men, says these things in these words: 'Oh light and truth,' with his own voice he openly confesses, just as you also have written, that there will be others who will come to you with similar powers, evil and magicians, and he names some Satan who contrives such things; therefore, he is not himself uncondemned, as if these things are not divine but are works of evil ones. But being forced by the truth, he has revealed both the things of others and examined the things concerning himself. How, therefore, is it not wicked to consider the one God and the others magicians from the same works? For what more than these things should the others, evil ones, be considered or this one, using the same witness, be thought to be? These things, indeed, he himself has acknowledged are not of a divine nature but of certain deceivers and thoroughly evil ones. See, therefore, if Celsus is not clearly refuted, doing evil to the word, saying one thing when Jesus speaks about those who will perform 'signs and wonders,' and another thing when the Jew according to Celsus says it. And for if Jesus were simply saying to the disciples to beware of those promising great deeds without specifying what they claim to be, perhaps his suspicion would have a place; but since Jesus warns us to beware of those who promise to be 'the Christ,' which magicians do not do, but also says that some living wickedly in the name of Jesus will perform powers and cast out demons of men, rather, if it must be said, the magic and every suspicion concerning them is proclaimed, and the divinity of Christ and the divinity of his disciples is introduced, because it is possible for someone using his name, and I do not know how, being worked upon by some power, to seem to perform similar things to Christ, and others, in the name of Jesus, to perform things similar to his genuine disciples.

bible_refs.note: do not believe, coming of the Son of Man

pass_b_english: Jesus therefore turns his disciples away not from simply ignoring magicians and those who promise to perform spectacular feats by whatever means (for his disciples had no need of such a warning) but from those who proclaim themselves to be the Christ of God and try, through certain pretenses, to draw Jesus' disciples to themselves. He does this in the passage where he says: "Then if anyone says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ,' or 'There he is,' do not believe it. For false christs and false prophets will arise and perform great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the elect. See, I have told you beforehand. So if they say to you, 'Look, he is in the wilderness,' do not go out; 'Look, he is in the inner rooms,' do not believe it. For as the lightning comes from the east and shines as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man" (Matt 24:24, 24:26-27). And in the passage where he says: "Many will say to me on that day, 'Lord, Lord, did we not eat in your name and drink in your name and cast out demons in your name and do many mighty works?' And then I will declare to them, 'Depart from me, for you are workers of lawlessness'" (Matt 7:22-23).

Celsus, however, wants to assimilate Jesus' mighty works to the magic practiced among men, and he puts it in these very words: "Oh light and truth," he openly confesses with his own voice, just as you also have written, that others will come to you with similar powers, evil men and magicians, and he names a certain Satan who contrives such things; so that he is not himself uncondemned, as if these works were not divine but the deeds of evil men. Yet, compelled by the truth, he has disclosed both the deeds of others and convicted himself. How then is it not wicked to judge the one as God and the others as magicians based on the same works? For why should the others be deemed evil rather than this one, when he uses the very same testimony? These things he himself has acknowledged are not marks of a divine nature but of certain deceivers and thoroughly wicked men.

Look, then, and see whether Celsus is not clearly refuted as one who corrupts the word, attributing one thing to Jesus when he speaks of those who will perform 'signs and wonders,' and another to the Jew in Celsus's narrative. For if Jesus had simply told his disciples to beware of those who promise mighty works without specifying what they claim to be, his suspicion might have had some foothold. But since Jesus warns us to beware of those who promise to be 'the Christ' — which magicians do not do — and also says that some living wickedly in the name of Jesus will perform mighty works and cast out demons, rather, if one must put it this way, magic and every suspicion about them is proclaimed false, and the divinity of Christ and the divinity of his disciples is vindicated. For it is possible that someone, using his name and I know not how energized by some power to pretend that he himself is the Christ, might seem to accomplish things similar to Christ, and that others, in the name of Jesus, might do things resembling those of his genuine disciples.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex Greek syntax, particularly the double negatives and the conditional arguments in the final section. Pass A maintains the literal structure (e.g., 'not from the not giving heed'), while Pass B provides a fluent rendering. Scripture citations in Pass B (Matt 24:24, 24:26-27, 7:22-23) correctly identify the quoted/alluded passages from the Greek text.
